design_decisions_beyond_the_pinned_spec: resolver.snapshot() for the dynamic resolver mints a brand-new, non-identity-equal _DynamicRootGraphSnapshot token on every call (confirmed by reading NonAuthorizingDynamicRootGraph.snapshot(), which always does `object.__new__(_DynamicRootGraphSnapshot)`), unlike the fixed resolver's idempotent cached singleton. Copying the fixed contract's `snapshot = resolver.snapshot()` / `resolver.snapshot()` pattern verbatim into the dynamic contract's _prepare/_verify would therefore make the binding-tuple equality check in _verify spuriously fail (each call re-derives a fresh, non-equal token) even for a genuinely-matching request. _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare and _verify instead read the resolver's already-current cached `resolver._snapshot` attribute (after a cheap `_p4_snapshot_integrity` re-check), matching exactly what commit_p4_batch's own locked critical section and _dynamic_p4_close_admission already use throughout -- never triggering a second, redundant graph re-derivation. This was discovered empirically during GREEN (a genuine 'P4 prepared candidate binding refused' failure on the first correctly-constructed positive-path attempt) and is disclosed here as a deliberate, necessary correction to the literal 'exactly as the fixed contract does' phrasing, not a deviation from the ADR's actual intent (which explicitly prioritizes exactly this kind of same-instance, no-extra-graph-read behavior throughout Decision point 6).

_DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract._prepare's signing-basis refs (tuple_refs/pce_refs) and its captured-receipt's consumer_kind/consumer_id/planned_capture_set_sha256 fields have no literal ADR-pinned source, because the dynamic domain has no resolvable 'cas' or 'planned-capture-entry' artifact reference (cas/pce are reconstructed in-memory, never stored). tuple_refs uses [admission_ref, root_pis_ref, dataset_g1_ref, dataset_g2_ref] (4 real refs, one fewer than the fixed contract's 5, since there is no separate resolvable cas ref in this domain); pce_refs is built the identical way the fixed contract already builds it (from entry['planned_entry_sha256'], no resolver lookup needed); consumer_kind is fixed to 'action' (matching subject_ref); consumer_id and planned_capture_set_sha256 use admission['run_id'] and admission_ref['sha256'] respectively, the closest available exact identifiers in this narrower chain. This is internally self-consistent and provably correct for the batch's own safety property (test item 5: _verify_bytes re-derives via the identical _prepare call and compares raw bytes, so any internal inconsistency would refuse, not silently pass) but is a genuine implementer judgment call the ADR text left open; flagged here for the record per the convergence-checkpoint disclosure convention.
